 Singapore Haze Update: PM2.5 Briefly Rises Before Returning to Normal
 The city skyline is seen through clear skies on Oct 27, 2026, as haze conditions improve in Singapore. (Photo: AFP/Roslan Rahman) Western Singapore records elevated pollution before showers help keep regional haze subdued.
 Air quality in western Singapore briefly worsened on November 1 as fine-particle pollution rose into the elevated range before returning to normal later in the day. The National Environment Agency expects continued showers across the region to help keep haze conditions subdued over the following days.
 Western Singapore Briefly Hits Elevated Range 
The one-hour PM2.5 reading in western Singapore entered the elevated range early on November 1, reaching 59 at 5 a.m. and 6 a.m. It later returned to normal, and by 5 p.m., one-hour PM2.5 readings across Singapore’s five regions ranged from 15 to 41. Under Singapore’s system, readings of up to 55 are considered normal, while 56 to 150 are classified as elevated.
 PSI Remains Within Moderate Band 
Despite the temporary PM2.5 increase, Singapore’s 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index remained in the moderate range. At 5 p.m. on November 1, readings ranged from 71 to 89 across the country. Air quality had remained within the good-to-moderate range since 11 p.m. on October 25 following an earlier period of more severe haze conditions.
 Smoke Plumes Remain Over Kalimantan 
The National Environment Agency said localized moderate to dense smoke plumes were still observed in Kalimantan on November 1. However, showers also occurred over northern, western, and eastern Singapore, while rainfall across parts of the surrounding region helped limit the movement and persistence of haze.
 Showers Expected to Suppress Haze 
NEA forecast Singapore’s 24-hour PSI to remain in the moderate range of 51 to 80 on November 2. The agency said showers over Sumatra, Kalimantan, Singapore, and surrounding areas were expected to keep haze conditions subdued. Easterly or southeasterly winds were forecast for November 3 and 4, but continuing showers were expected to reduce the likelihood of significant haze affecting Singapore.
 Residents Advised to Monitor Hourly Readings 
NEA advised residents to use the 24-hour PSI forecast when planning activities for the following day and the one-hour PM2.5 reading when deciding on immediate outdoor activities. When PM2.5 enters the elevated range, healthy people are advised to reduce strenuous outdoor activity for that hour, while children, older adults, pregnant women, and people with chronic heart or lung conditions should avoid strenuous outdoor activity.
 Singapore’s brief PM2.5 increase shows that air quality can still fluctuate even as the broader haze situation improves. For Singaporeans, continued monitoring remains important while smoke persists elsewhere in the region. For Indonesians, particularly communities in fire-affected parts of Sumatra and Kalimantan, regional rainfall and changing wind conditions remain closely connected to both local smoke exposure and the potential movement of haze toward neighboring countries.
